names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 27 mai, «Sfântul Mucenic Iuliu Veteranul».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 26 Μαΐου, «Άγιος Ιούλιος ο Μάρτυρας», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 25. мај ст. ст., „Свети мученици Пасикрат, Валентион, Јулије и други“ — Свети is not a rank, мученици is the `martyr` this corpus puts in `types`, and the other names in the heading are his companions and not his own. **„Ветеран“ is left out of the form although the display name keeps it**: in this book it is not an epithet in the heading at all but the man’s own word about himself in the body, „Ја сам ветеран“, and one `sr` form per folder means the heading’s form and not a composed one. **Measured**: `foldchk.py` returns `NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM` for «Јулије», so this is the first folder to hold it, and `julius-of-aegina` is the only other Julius in the corpus. The Greek form on this folder, «Ιούλιος», is the same bare name; the Romanian, «Iuliu Veteranul», keeps the epithet because doxologia’s line prints it.

death.note: doxologia.ro's life opens «În timpul persecuției împăraților Dioclețian (284-305) și Maximian Galeriu (305-311)» and dates the decree that removed Christian soldiers from the army to after the victory over the Persians «în anul 297». The page states no year for his death; the interval recorded is the span of the two reigns it does print.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 27 mai — «Sfântul Mucenic Iuliu Veteranul»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 26ης Μαΐου — «Άγιος Ιούλιος ο Μάρτυρας»

attestations.note: **saint.gr keeps him on 26 Μαΐου where doxologia.ro keeps him on 27 mai, one day apart, and the row records the day page that was read.** The identification is not in doubt: both accounts give a soldier of the Roman army at **Durostorum in Moesia**, brought before the governor **Maximus**, pressed to sacrifice, refusing, and beheaded; the folder's own life already has all four of those from the Romanian side. The Greek adds a flat year the Romanian page does not give, «καταδικάσθηκε στον δι' αποκεφαλισμού θάνατο το 302 μ.Χ., επί αυτοκράτορα Διοκλητιανού (284 - 305 μ.Χ.)», and the head line repeats it; **the folder's `dates` is left as it is**, an interval «between 284 and 311» that a reader does not replace from an upgrade file, and the Greek's 302 is recorded here and in the added paragraph so that a later reader can lift it with a citation. The Greek also links him to three saints of another day — «συνδεόταν με τους αγίους Πασικράτη, Βαλεντίωνα και Ησύχιο, που μαρτύρησαν νωρίτερα (τιμούνται 24 Απριλίου)» — and the corpus keeps none of the three, so none is linked. No hymn is printed.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 07.06.2026 (25. мај ст. ст.) — „Свети мученици Пасикрат, Валентион, Јулије и други“

attestations.note: The day’s third entry, whose heading names him third. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of the 23, 24 and 25 May is. **THE COMPANY, AND HOW IT WAS TOLD FROM THE OTHER DAYS.** The heading enumerates three — „Пасикрат, Валентион, Јулије“ — and „и други“ after them, and the body names two more, **Никандар** and **Маркијан**, so five men of this entry have folders and all five get a row. **The corpus keeps them on three different days of three different calendars**: `passicrates-of-durostorum` and `valentine-of-durostorum` on 24 April, `julius-the-veteran` on the Romanian 27 May and the Greek 26 May, and `nicander-of-durostorum` and `marcian-of-durostorum` on 8 June. **Not one of them was found by `sr-namesweep.mjs` scoring this heading** — it scores only the first name of an enumerated company, which is its fourth known failure mode — **and not one of them is on the day list for the menologion 25/5 either**, the corpus keeping none of them on that day. They were found by `ls saints | grep -iE 'pasicrat|valent|nicander|marcian|julius' and by grepping the corpus for the entry’s own uncommon proper name, Durostorum, which returned twelve folders at once. **The grep beat both instruments again**, and the misspelling is why the first grep missed one: the corpus stores him `passicrates-of-durostorum`, with two s. **«Доростолу Македонском» AGAINST MOESIA, RECORDED AND NOT RESOLVED.** The Prologue puts Durostorum in **Macedonia**; doxologia puts it in the Roman province of Moesia Inferior and saint.gr in Moesia. **No `locations` was written or changed on any of the five.** **«око 302» IS REFUSED ON ALL FIVE, AND FOR THREE DIFFERENT REASONS.** It is the only year this entry gives, it is approximate, and it is stated of the heading’s company and not of any one man. For `julius-the-veteran` it **narrows**: his folder holds 284 to 311 off the Romanian page, and a reader before this one had already refused saint.gr’s flat 302 for the same reason, writing „the year is the Greek’s; this folder’s dating stays the interval the Romanian page allows“ — this book agreeing with saint.gr changes nothing, two books inside a range still not narrowing it. For `nicander-of-durostorum` and `marcian-of-durostorum` it would **widen an `attested` 298 with an approximation**, and a „око“ is not a source for an endpoint. For `passicrates-of-durostorum` and `valentine-of-durostorum` **it is the Prologue’s second answer to a question the Prologue has already answered differently**, and that is the finding of the day, below. **NO DATE ON ANY OF THE FIVE WAS TOUCHED.** **A THIRD DAY, ON A THIRD CALENDAR**: doxologia keeps him on 27 May, saint.gr on 26 May, and this book on 25 May. Three calendars, three consecutive days, and **each row carries its own day**, which is what the schema is for; nothing was moved and no day was reconciled. The day list for the menologion 25/5 could not see him, and the namesweep scoring this heading could not either. **New here, and it is the sentence the Romanian page summarises and this one quotes**: that **Julius said at the trial „Ја сам ветеран, двадесет шест година служио сам верно цару, па кад сам до сада био веран нижем, како сад да не будем веран вишем?“** — I am a veteran, twenty-six years I served the emperor faithfully, and if I have been faithful until now to the lesser, how should I not be faithful to the greater? — **and that the greater is the heavenly Emperor, which the Prologue glosses in its own voice.** The twenty-six years are new: neither other page gives a length of service, and **they are a duration and no year is derived from them.** `martyr` and `soldier` are both corroborated — „Војници римски“ and the veteran’s own word. **FOUR NEW `related` ROWS, ALL RECIPROCAL, AND THIS FOLDER HAD NONE AT ALL.** Its `related` was empty although **its own life already names Pasicrate, Valentin and Hesychius in prose** off doxologia and saint.gr — `related-floor.test.mjs` does not match those forms, so nothing caught it. The 25 May entry narrates one martyrdom for five men, which is the test that owes a row, so `passicrates-of-durostorum`, `valentine-of-durostorum`, `nicander-of-durostorum` and `marcian-of-durostorum` are added and this folder is added on each of theirs. **`hesychius-of-durostorum` is NOT added**: this entry does not name him, and a row is owed for what the body narrates, not for what another book says about the same men. **That is a gap this day deliberately leaves open** — his life and Julius’s are tied together on saint.gr, and the row is the author’s to write off those pages, not this reader’s to write off a book that is silent. No `locations`. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the Romanian one on this folder stays.

hymns.text: Cu podoaba virtuților strălucind și împodobit cu lumina muceniciei fiind, Sfinte Iuliu, strălucești mai mult decât soarele, diamantule slăvit, luminând pe cei ce-ți fac cu dragoste pomenirea cea delumină-purtătoare, de-Hristos încununatule.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfântului Mucenic Iuliu Veteranul

english.text: Shining with the adornment of the virtues and arrayed in the light of martyrdom, holy Julius, thou shinest brighter than the sun, O glorious diamond, giving light to those who keep with love thy light-bearing memory, thou who art crowned by Christ.
